--- license: mit library_name: transformers pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text --- # DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017

Technical Report 👁️

## Introduction **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017** is a minor update to [**DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. Alongside these gains, the model reduces task execution time and output length, enabling users to complete tasks faster and at lower cost and advancing the performance–cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses.
| Benchmark | DS-V4.1-Flash-1017 | DS-V4.1-Flash | K3 | GLM-5.3 | GPT-5.6 Sol | Opus 5 | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | HLE w/o tools | 42.6 (44.0†) | 36.8 (39.1†) | 43.5 | 42.0† | 44.5 | 56.3 | | Terminal-Bench 4.0 | 42.3 | 31.2 | 12.6 | 37.9 | 39.9 | 51.8 | | DeepSWE v1.1 | 77.0 | 74.2 | 67.5 | 66.9 | 73.0 | 74.0 | | ProgramBench | 29.1 | 20.3 | 17.5 | 19.0 | 23.0 | 37.0 | | NL2Repo-Bench | 68.2 | 65.4 | 58.0 | 58.0 | 56.8 | 75.3 | | Automation-Bench v1.0.6 | 60.5 | 54.8 | 46.7 | 48.8 | 45.8 | 50.3 | | Agents’ Last Exam | 35.4 | 31.8 | 27.6 | 28.5 | 26.7 | 28.6 | | Apex Bench v1.1 | 72.1 | 64.6 | 47.8 | 56.6 | 54.3 | 65.8 | | Chartography (w/tools) | 83.0 | 78.9 | 68.1 | — | 79.9 | 84.0 | | BabyVision (w/tools) | 92.5 | 89.6 | 85.7 | — | 88.9 | 94.1 | | ZeroBench-main (w/tools) | 51.0 | 49.0 | 41.0 | — | 53.0 | 52.0 |
*† denotes the text-only subset of HLE. We use the Claude Code harness for Terminal-Bench 4.0 and the Mini-SWE-V2 harness for DeepSWE v1.1.* ## Prompt Encoding This release does not include a Jinja-format chat template. The [`encoding`](encoding/README.md) folder contains a self-contained Python reference implementation (`encoding.py`) with test cases for multi-turn conversations, tool calling, thinking mode, numeric reasoning effort, mid-conversation system messages, and interleaved image content. For production use, we additionally release [deepseek-recipe](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe), a set of Rust libraries with Python bindings that provides the same prompt format as a maintained, protocol-aware toolkit. It converts Messages, Chat Completions, and Responses API requests into the Conversation format, encodes them into DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 prompts or token IDs, and parses model output back into complete or streamed responses — covering thinking, tool calls, images, and generation settings. Model inference, tool execution, and HTTP transport are left to the caller. ## Minimal Inference Please refer to the [`inference`](inference/README.md) folder for instructions on weight conversion and running inference locally. **Recommended sampling parameters:** | Parameter | Value | | :--- | :--- | | `temperature` | 1.0 | | `top_p` | 1.0 | | `context_window` | 1M tokens | | `max_tokens` | ≥ 256K | ## License This repository and the model weights are licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{deepseekai2026deepseekv41flash, title={DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression}, author={DeepSeek-AI}, year={2026}, } ``` ## Contact If you have any questions, please raise an issue or contact us at [service@deepseek.com](mailto:service@deepseek.com).

# 1. Introduction In Nanbeige4.3, we take a foundational step toward pushing the boundaries of lightweight agents. Our strategy centers on building a high-capacity teacher agent first, which will subsequently anchor the distillation of advanced agentic capabilities into smaller models. To this end, we first introduce Nanbeige4.3-33B, designed as the flagship teacher model for the Nanbeige4.3 series. Delivering state-of-the-art agentic performance among open models in the ~30B parameter class, Nanbeige4.3-33B excels at complex coding and professional cowork tasks. It not only offers a powerful, cost-effective option for immediate real-world deployment, but also lays the necessary foundation to power our upcoming small model distillation pipeline (e.g., for Nanbeige4.3-3B).
# 2. Model Performance We compare Nanbeige4.3-33B with recently released frontier models at around the 30B-parameter scale: Qwen3.8-27B, Muse-Glimmer-30B, and Gemma4-31B. All models are evaluated at their highest thinking effort. For each benchmark, we use the same inference hyperparameters and harness across models.

models.name: flint
models.readme_content:
--- license: apache-2.0 library_name: transformers pipeline_tag: text-generation ---

Recursive Flint

Blog | Hugging Face | Local engine | Documentation

Flint is Recursive’s mixture-of-experts language model for coding agents, with 39.8 billion total parameters and approximately 2.5 billion active per token. It is designed to investigate codebases, fix bugs, implement features, and write tests. Flint supports text input and output, reasoning, and multi-turn tool use. In our release evaluations, it scores 54.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 89.7% on SWE-bench Pro v2, and 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified. This repository contains the BF16 checkpoint, model configuration, tokenizer, chat template, and an SGLang serving kit. Quantized variants are prepared separately for NVIDIA and Apple Silicon runtimes. ## Evaluation ![Flint benchmark performance: BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints compared with local models that run on similar hardware](assets/flint_benchmarks_nvfp4.png) Flint results use temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20. Terminal-Bench uses Terminus 2; SWE-bench uses mini-swe-agent. Agentic scores report average pass@1 over at least five attempts. † marks scores measured by Recursive; other comparison scores are developer-reported. Evaluation setups vary across sources. Flint’s Terminal-Bench score counts solutions obtained through web retrieval as unsuccessful; developer-reported scores may not apply the same adjustment. ## Model specifications | Property | Flint | | :---- | :---- | | Developer | Recursive | | Architecture | Decoder-only mixture-of-experts Transformer | | Total parameters | 39.8B | | Active parameters per token | Approximately 2.5B, including the output head¹ | | Layers | 49: 2 dense layers followed by 47 MoE layers | | Attention | 35 sliding-window layers and 14 full-attention layers | | Sliding window | 513 tokens: the current token and 512 preceding tokens | | Attention heads | 32 query heads and 4 key/value heads; head dimension 128 | | Attention normalization | Per-head QK RMSNorm and learned per-head attention sinks | | Position encoding | RoPE on sliding-window layers; no positional encoding on full-attention layers | | Experts per MoE layer | 256 routed experts, with 6 selected per token, plus an always-active shared expert | | Documented context configuration | 262,144 tokens, including prompt and generated output | | Vocabulary | 150,144 tokens | | Input / output | Text / text | | Stated knowledge cutoff | June 2026 | ¹ The active-parameter convention includes the output head and excludes the full input embedding matrix. The active body alone is approximately 2.2B parameters. “40B-A2.5B” is the rounded model-size designation. ## Getting started Flint runs on one B300 or H200 GPU per replica with the SGLang kit in `sglang/`. Transformers modeling code is not included yet. ```bash pip install -U huggingface_hub openai hf download RecursiveSI/flint --local-dir flint && cd flint # about 80 GB docker build -t flint-sglang sglang docker run -d --name flint --gpus '"device=0"' --ipc=host -p 127.0.0.1:30000:30000 \ -v "$PWD:/model" -e MODEL=/model flint-sglang bash /model/sglang/serve_b300.sh # H200: serve_h200.sh until curl -sf localhost:30000/health_generate >/dev/null; do sleep 15; done # progress: docker logs -f flint python3 sglang/example_client.py --base-url http://localhost:30000/v1 # reasoning and a tool call ``` ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:30000/v1", api_key="unused") response = client.chat.completions.create( model="flint", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a Python function that merges overlapping intervals."}], max_tokens=32768, ) print(response.choices[0].message.content) ``` [`sglang/README.md`](sglang/README.md) covers requirements, serve-script options, multi-GPU deployments, and API details. ### Recommended generation settings | Setting | Value | | :---- | :---- | | Temperature | 1.0 | | Top-p / top-k | 0.95 / 20 | | Output budget for hard problems | At least 32768 tokens, including reasoning | The server applies these sampling settings when a request omits them. Flint supports OpenAI-compatible tool calls. Use the checkpoint’s chat template and preserve returned `reasoning_content` in conversation history. Prompt and output share the context window. ## Training Flint was trained from scratch through pretraining, mid-training, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. Training includes text and code, instruction following, and agentic tasks. ## Limitations and responsible use Flint’s supervised fine-tuning included safety-oriented examples, but the model can still produce incorrect or harmful content, faulty code, or inappropriate tool calls. Test generated code and review consequential changes before applying them. Tool-using applications should enforce their own permissions and execution boundaries; structured tool-call grammar does not prevent the model from choosing an unsafe or incorrect action. Long reasoning can increase latency and exhaust the output budget before an answer is complete. The context configuration is a capacity limit, not a guarantee of uniform accuracy across all sequence lengths or tasks. Results can vary with checkpoint precision and inference runtime; evaluate the specific checkpoint and runtime you intend to deploy. ## License and reporting Flint is released under the [Apache 2.0 license](LICENSE). Hosted API terms and data practices are separate from the weight license. For model and serving issues, contact support@recursive.co
models.description: Flint is a 39.8B parameter Mixture-of-Experts language model optimized for coding agents, capable of code investigation, bug fixing, feature implementation, and test generation. It excels in reasoning and multi-turn tool use, achieving high scores on benchmarks like SWE-bench.

models.readme_content:
--- license: apache-2.0 language: - en - zh library_name: transformers pipeline_tag: text-generation tags: - llm - sparkx2_5 base_model: - XHToken/Spark-X2.6-4B-Base --- # Spark-X2.6-4B: Advancing the Frontier of On-Device Agents for Real-World Tasks
[![Slack](https://img.shields.io/badge/Slack-Join-4A154B?logo=slack&logoColor=white)](https://join.slack.com/t/tokenspark/shared_invite/zt-432qf8l2f-5~dLyXv8uETr0P0UuC07nw) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/kTDE2Hg8aw) [![YouTube](https://img.shields.io/badge/YouTube-Subscribe-FF0000?logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/@SparkLLM) [![dev.to](https://img.shields.io/badge/dev.to-Follow-0A0A0A?logo=devdotto&logoColor=white)](https://dev.to/sparkllm) [![Bluesky](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bluesky-Follow-0285FF?logo=bluesky&logoColor=white)](https://bsky.app/profile/sparkllm.bsky.social) [![X](https://img.shields.io/badge/X-Follow-000000?logo=x&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/sparkllm) [![Zhihu](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zhihu-Follow-0084FF?logo=zhihu&logoColor=white)](https://www.zhihu.com/people/zhiikz7qh7m) [![WeChat](https://img.shields.io/badge/WeChat-Join-07C160?logo=wechat&logoColor=white)](images/xhtoken-wechat.jpg)
> [!Note] > This repository contains model weights and configuration files for the post-trained model in the Hugging Face Transformers format.

## Introduction A little over a month has passed since Spark-X2.5. In the rapidly evolving world of AI agents, that is enough time to rethink, refine, and move the frontier forward. Building on the Spark-X2.5-4B, we introduce **Spark-X2.6-4B**, the latest generation of our compact, general-purpose language models for on-device deployment. Spark-X2.6-4B retains exactly the same architecture as Spark-X2.5-4B, achieving its capability gains through improved post-training. It delivers substantial improvements in coding, agent, long-context, multilingual, reasoning, etc. These advances enable more capable and practical on-device AI for developers and users tackling real-world tasks. **Technical Highlights**: - **Stronger Coding, Agentic, and Long-Context Capabilities**: The models deliver substantial improvements in agentic workflows involving complex tool use, multi-step planning, and software engineering. They achieve state-of-the-art performance among similarly sized open-source models, matching or even surpassing models with approximately 9B parameters. - **Controllable Thinking Budget**: The models provide three configurable thinking levels—none, low, high—allowing applications to balance reasoning quality, latency, and inference cost dynamically. ## Benchmarks We evaluate our models and compare them with leading on-device models of similar size across a broad range of tasks, including agent, code, math, general and knowledge. Spark-X2.6-4B achieves best-in-class performance among models of comparable size, while matching or exceeding the performance of larger 9B models on several benchmarks.

## Edge Inference Spark-X2.6-4B delivers inference efficiency on par with or better than comparable on-device models, including Qwen3.5-4B and Gemma-E4B. It combines this efficiency with stronger capabilities, making it a practical choice for responsive, resource-conscious on-device AI.

## Quickstart ### Transformers Install the required version with `pip install transformers==4.57.1`. ```python from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer model_id = "XHToken/Spark-X2.6-4B" tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( model_id, trust_remote_code=True, torch_dtype="auto", device_map="auto", ) messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of Anhui Province?"}] inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template( messages, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True, return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt", ).to(model.device) outputs = model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=131072, do_sample=True, temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=0, ) print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)) ``` ### SGLang The examples below serve a local Spark-X2.6-4B checkpoint. Set `MODEL_PATH` to its absolute path before starting a container: ```bash export MODEL_PATH=/absolute/path/to/Spark-X2.6-4B ``` #### Install SGLang Use the pre-built image that tracks the Spark-X2.6 runtime: ##### For NVIDIA GPUs: ```bash docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260827-20621aa1 ``` ##### For Ascend NPUs: ```bash # A3 daily build export SGLANG_IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/sglang:main-cann9.0.0-a3 # A2 daily build (use this instead on A2 hardware) export SGLANG_IMAGE=quay.io/ascend/sglang:main-cann9.0.0-910b docker pull "$SGLANG_IMAGE" ``` #### Run Inference The following commands start an OpenAI-compatible API server configured for a maximum context length of 1,048,576 tokens. This setting requires sufficient device memory; reduce `--context-length` when necessary. #### Server ##### NVIDIA GPU: ```bash docker run --rm -it \ --gpus '"device=0"' \ --ipc=host \ -p 30000:30000 \ -v "$MODEL_PATH:/root/Spark-X2.6-4B:ro" \ lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260827-20621aa1 \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /root/Spark-X2.6-4B \ --served-model-name spark2.6 \ --tool-call-parser spark25 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tp-size 1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --context-length 1048576 \ --chat-template /root/Spark
models.description: Spark-X2.6-4B is a compact, general-purpose language model optimized for on-device deployment, excelling in coding, agentic workflows, and long-context tasks with controllable thinking budgets for balanced performance and efficiency.

models.readme_content:
--- library_name: transformers tags: - translation language: - zh - en - fr - pt - es - ja - tr - ru - ar - ko - th - it - de - vi - ms - id - tl - hi - pl - cs - nl - km - my - fa - gu - ur - te - mr - he - bn - ta - uk - bo - kk - mn - ug license: apache-2.0 --- **English** | [简体中文](README_CN.md)

A Low-Latency, High-Quality Model for Real-Time Simultaneous Translation

[![Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hugging%20Face-Tencent%20Hy-ffc107)](https://huggingface.co/collections/tencent/hy-simulmt) [![ModelScope](https://img.shields.io/badge/ModelScope-Tencent%20Hy-624aff)](https://www.modelscope.cn/collections/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-SimulMT) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Hy--SimulMT-181717?logo=github)](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-SimulMT)
## Introduction **Hy-SimulMT** is a real-time simultaneous translation model developed by Tencent Hunyuan, supporting **bidirectional speech-to-speech translation between Chinese and English**. It continuously receives incoming audio and translates as the speaker talks, producing both translated text and speech. With **real-time voice cloning**, it preserves the speaker's vocal characteristics while conveying the message accurately. Designed for live communication settings such as meetings, speeches, and interviews, Hy-SimulMT aims to convey information accurately while reducing the disruption that waiting introduces into a conversation. To evaluate this balance between translation quality and response speed, we combine public benchmarks, real-world audio, and comparisons with professional simultaneous interpreters. In our **RealSI long-form audio evaluation**, Hy-SimulMT achieved a **StreamLAAL of approximately 3 seconds**, the lowest among the systems shown in the comparison. Its GEMBA score exceeded those of the compared open-source models and four of the five commercial APIs. The [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-SimulMT) provides the **SimulInfer inference service** and **SimulTrain training tools**. Speech output and voice cloning require a configured TTS service. You can also try Hy-SimulMT in the **Hy Translate App**.

Scan to download the Hy Translate App

Android iOS
## News - **2026.10.26 | Release**: Hy-SimulMT is released with bidirectional real-time simultaneous translation between Chinese and English and real-time voice cloning. Project and model resources are linked below. ## Results ### Keeping Up Faster, Conveying Meaning More Accurately The challenge of simultaneous translation is not simply to convert one language into another, but to understand and formulate a translation while the speaker is still talking. Waiting for more information often helps resolve the complete meaning, but also makes listeners wait longer. Speaking earlier, on the other hand, places greater demands on incremental understanding and translation generation. Hy-SimulMT focuses on this balance between quality and latency: **translating as a continuous audio stream arrives, so that listeners receive information promptly while the original meaning is preserved as accurately as possible.** We compared Hy-SimulMT with several open-source simultaneous translation models and commercial APIs on the open-source RealSI long-form audio benchmark. The results show that Hy-SimulMT achieves competitive translation quality at lower latency.
*The horizontal axis shows StreamLAAL, a measure of streaming translation lag, in seconds (lower is better); the vertical axis shows the GEMBA translation quality score (higher is better). StreamLAAL is not the same as the time to first speech output.* In this evaluation, Hy-SimulMT achieved a **StreamLAAL of approximately 3 seconds**, the lowest among the systems shown. Its GEMBA score exceeded those of the compared open-source models and four of the five commercial APIs. These results suggest that lower latency does not necessarily require a substantial sacrifice in translation quality. Hy-SimulMT offers a more timely way to access cross-language information during extended speeches, interviews, and meetings. ### From Public Benchmarks to Real-World Settings #### Translation Quality on Multiple Short-Form Audio Benchmarks In addition to long-form audio, we evaluated the model on four public short-form audio benchmarks—FLEURS, CoVoST2, ACL6060, and RealSI-Sentence—to examine translation performance under different data conditions. | API / Model | FLEURS | CoVoST2 | ACL6060 | RealSI-Sentence | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Qwen3.8-LiveTranslate | 88.4 | **82.1** | 80.5 | 84.4 | | **Hy-SimulMT** | **90.3** | **75.5** | **81.2** | **84.7** | | Gemini3.5-LiveTranslate | **92.4** | 74.4 | **82.6** | 82.2 | | Confucius4 R2T2 → T3PO | 89.4 | 76.8 | 76.1 | 77.7 | | Seed-LiveInterpret2.0 | 85.8 | 67.7 | 74.8 | 80.0 | | SimulS2ST-Omni | 78.6 | 66.6 | 73.1 | 77.4 | | GPT-Realtime-Translate | 77.7 | 50.8 | 76.4 | 76.7 | | XunFei-Simult-Interpretation | 73.4 | 57.0 | 57.5 | 70.9 | | SeamlessStreaming | 72.8 | 60.9 | 49.8 | 56.9 | *Higher scores are better. The entire Hy-SimulMT row is bolded to highlight our model; other bolded values indicate
models.description: Hy-SimulMT-30B-A3B-FP8 is a low-latency, high-quality model for real-time bidirectional speech-to-speech translation between Chinese and English. It features continuous audio stream processing, real-time voice cloning, and achieves a StreamLAAL of ~3 seconds, making it ideal for live meetings, speeches, and interviews.

# LFM3-1.7B LFM3-1.7B is a **text model for local agents and specialized applications**, based on our new tri-hybrid architecture. - **Agentic training:** post-trained for agentic harnesses such as Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenClaw, with a 256K-token context window. - **Designed for the edge:** at 4-bit precision, it takes about 1 GB of memory, so it fits on any phone or laptop. - **Made to be specialized:** adapt the model to your domains, formats, and tools via quick single-GPU fine-tuning. Find more information about the LFM3 family in [our release blog post](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm3). ## Model details
The [LFM3 family](https://huggingface.co/collections/LiquidAI/lfm3) includes base, text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models.
Property Specification
Checkpoint Post-trained, text-only language model
Parameters 1.73B
Architecture 24 layers: 13 gated short convolutions, 5 sliding-window attention, 6 global attention
Context length 256K tokens (input + output)
Vocabulary 128,000 tokens
Languages English, Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish, Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, Hindi, Russian, Polish
License LFM Open License v1.0
LFM3-1.7B is designed for local agents, tool calling, structured outputs, and domain-specific fine-tuning. Use retrieval or search for knowledge-heavy tasks. It is not recommended for agentic coding or complex multi-step reasoning due to its small size. ## Inference

--- pipeline_tag: image-text-to-text license: other license_name: minimax-community license_link: LICENSE library_name: transformers tags: - multimodal - moe - agent - coding - video ---


**MiniMax-M3.1-Flash** is a native multimodal mixture-of-experts model for coding, agentic workflows, computer use, and cybersecurity. It supports text, image, and video inputs with a context window of up to **1M tokens**. Building on MiniMax-M3, M3.1-Flash improves task performance and inference efficiency with sparse attention throughout the model, quantization-aware training, and DSpark speculative decoding. **Highlights:** - **Agentic performance:** A generational leap in agentic tasks, coding, and cybersecurity — 76.2 on BankerToolBench, 73.7% on DeepSWE v1.1, 61.7 on OSWorld V2, 29.6 on Agents' Last Exam, and 82.2 on CyberGym. - **Efficient by design:** Sparse attention throughout, quantization-aware training, and DSpark speculative decoding improve inference efficiency. ## Model at a Glance - **Architecture:** Native multimodal mixture-of-experts (MoE) - **Parameters:** Approximately 428B total; 23B activated per token - **Inputs / output:** Text, image, and video inputs; text output - **Context window:** Up to 1,000,000 tokens - **Attention:** [MiniMax Sparse Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13392) (MSA) throughout the model - **Speculative decoding:** DSpark draft head included ## Benchmarks

# DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 · GSQ-RCO GGUFs **Non-uniform GGUF quantizations** of a 763B-parameter, 384-expert MoE, produced with **GSQ** and **RCO**. [![arXiv: GSQ](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-GSQ_2604.18556-b31b1b?logo=arxiv&logoColor=white)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18556) [![arXiv: RCO](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-RCO_2605.00649-b31b1b?logo=arxiv&logoColor=white)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00649) [![GSQ code](https://img.shields.io/badge/code-GSQ-181717?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/IST-DASLab/GSQ) [![RCO code](https://img.shields.io/badge/code-RCO-181717?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/IST-DASLab/RCO) [![DASLab](https://img.shields.io/badge/DASLab-GitHub-101048?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/IST-DASLab) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-19a34a)](#license)
![Base model vs GSQ-RCO quants on AIME25, GPQA-Diamond and LiveCodeBench v6](assets/plots/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-benchmarks_bars.png) > **Update, October 27, 2026.** The files now use llama.cpp's own DeepSeek-V4.1 layout and load in llama.cpp [b11870](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b11870) or newer, including images. > - **Downloaded the earlier files?** You do not need to download the model again. Run [convert_ds41_upstream.py](./convert_ds41_upstream.py) on your model folder: it rewrites the files locally into exactly the current ones and fetches only 80 KB. See [Updating an existing download](#updating-an-existing-download). > - **New download?** The shared Engram file is shard 6 of every build, so link it once per build you use (`` is `IQ1_M`, `IQ2_XXS` or `IQ2_XS`; see [llama.cpp](#llamacpp)): > > ```sh > ln -s DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Engram-IQ4_NL.gguf DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GSQ-RCO--00006-of-00006.gguf > ``` --- ## Overview This repository provides GGUF quantizations of **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017** at three sizes: **IQ1_M (1.75 bits per weight), IQ2_XXS (2.00) and IQ2_XS (2.25)**. In contrast to uniform quantization, which applies a single quantization type to all weight tensors, each model here assigns a separate quantization type to every tensor. The assignment is obtained by a gradient-based search that allocates precision according to per-tensor sensitivity, subject to a total size budget. The resulting files are standard GGUF. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with **763.2B parameters**: **384 routed experts per layer**, of which 6 are active per token, and a 1M-token context window. The routed experts dominate the parameter count, so they also dominate the size budget, and the search spends most of its freedom there, assigning a quantization type **per layer** (not per expert, which GGUF cannot express). With [Strata](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata), every build runs on a **single GPU with 12 GB of VRAM**. See [Usage](#usage). > **Method summary.** GSQ provides accurate low-bit scalar quantization of each tensor at a given quantization type; RCO assigns the per-tensor quantization types under a size budget. Together they yield a non-uniform GGUF at the requested size. | Method | Description | |---|---| | **GSQ** (Gumbel-Softmax Quantization, [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18556), [code](https://github.com/IST-DASLab/GSQ)) | Post-training scalar quantization that jointly learns the per-coordinate grid assignments and the per-group scales via a Gumbel-Softmax relaxation. GSQ closes most of the gap between scalar and vector quantization at 2 to 3 bits while remaining deployable in standard scalar formats such as GGUF. | | **RCO** (Riemannian Constrained Optimization, [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00649), [code](https://github.com/IST-DASLab/RCO)) | Assigns one of K quantization types to each of N tensors under a total size budget. The budget constraint is reformulated as a smooth Riemannian manifold in logit space, which permits gradient-based optimization directly on the task loss while enforcing the budget exactly, without constraint-specific hyperparameter tuning. | Both methods were developed at the [Deep Algorithms and Systems Lab (DASLab)](https://github.com/IST-DASLab), Institute of Science and Technology Austria. --- ## Available files Each build is a backbone GGUF in five shards, named after its quantization identifier: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GSQ-RCO--0000i-of-00006.gguf`, i = 1 to 5. Shard 1 holds the metadata only, shards 2 to 5 the transformer weights, **551.9B parameters**. The bpw is the average bit-width over these, which is what the search controls. The **Engram file**, `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-Engram-IQ4_NL.gguf`, holds the model's two Engram lookup tables (196.6B parameters) at IQ4_NL, 4.50 bpw. It is identical for all builds, so it is stored once and needs to be downloaded only once, also when trying several builds. llama.cpp loads it as shard 6 of a build, so each build needs a link to it named `...--00006-of-00006.gguf` (one command, see [llama.cpp](#llamacpp)). The tables are a lookup, not a matmul weight, so they are held at a fixed type in every build and excluded from the search. They are quantized in the evaluated models, not just the shipped ones. | Build | bpw | Backbone | Engram | Total | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `IQ1_M` | 1.75 | 120.72 GB | 110.60 GB | 231.32 GB | Smallest | | `IQ2_XXS` | 2.00 | 138.24 GB | 110.60 GB | 248.84 GB | Recommended; closest to the base model | | `IQ2_XS` | 2.25 | 155.23 GB | 110.60 GB | 265.83 GB | | All three builds run on

# FLUX 3 Image Klein for ComfyUI

![Launch gallery](./launch-gallery.jpg)

FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6B open weights model for text-to-image generation and image editing. It takes a prompt and up to 10 reference images and returns one image. Text-to-image, single-reference edits and multi-reference compositions run through the same model, with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct as the text encoder.

The 5.6B parameter label refers to the image transformer; the text encoder is separate.

This repository holds the model files repackaged for [ComfyUI](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI): the distilled and base transformers in BF16, int8 and NVFP4, the text encoder in BF16 and int8, the prompt upsampler in BF16, int8 and w4a8, and the image autoencoder. The original model repositories are [FLUX 3 Image Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein), [FLUX 3 Image Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) and [FLUX 3 Image Klein Prompt Upsampler](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup).

Inference code, prompt upsampling and the bounding box format: [black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) on GitHub.

**Do not use the model without a prompt upsampler.** FLUX 3 Image Klein takes full scene captions, for text-to-image, editing and layout with boxes alike; a short prompt sent as typed gives generic output. Use ours, the `qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_int8_convrot.safetensors` file in this repository, which the workflows run by default (see [Using with ComfyUI](#using-with-comfyui)), or any LLM you prefer with a system prompt that expands the request into one full scene caption ([`system_prompts.json`](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup/blob/main/system_prompts.json) has ours).

| Checkpoint | Format | Steps | Guidance | Built for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Klein Base](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base) | undistilled, bfloat16 | 50 | 3.5 | fine-tuning, LoRA training, research |
| [Klein](https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein) | distilled, bfloat16 | 16 | none | generation and editing, self-hosting; the checkpoint behind the BFL API |

## Key Features

1. Text-to-image, single-reference editing and multi-reference generation in one model.
2. Bounding boxes in the prompt. Place elements with boxes on a 0 to 1000 grid, then recolor, move, replace or remove them through the prompt. Boxes guide placement and scale; they do not constrain pixels to a hard mask.
3. Text rendering within generated images.
4. Released under the [FLUX Kommunity License](LICENSE.md). The license permits non-commercial use and provides a commercial-output exception for Qualifying Users, subject to its terms. See [License](#license) below.

## Files

Place the files in the following folders:

```
📂 ComfyUI/
└── 📂 models/
    ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-base-bf16.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-base-int8-convrot.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-base-nvfp4.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-bf16.safetensors
    │   ├── flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot.safetensors
    │   └── flux3-image-klein-nvfp4.safetensors
    ├── 📂 text_encoders/
    │   ├── qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_bf16.safetensors
    │   ├── qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_int8_convrot.safetensors
    │   ├── qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_w4a8.safetensors
    │   ├── qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors
    │   └── qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors
    └── 📂 vae/
        └── flux2-vae.safetensors
```

Files with `-base-` in the name are the base checkpoint; the others are the distilled checkpoint.

| File | Content | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-bf16.safetensors` | Klein, distilled, BF16 | 11.1 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot.safetensors` | Klein, distilled, int8 | 5.8 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-nvfp4.safetensors` | Klein, distilled, NVFP4 | 5.3 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-base-bf16.safetensors` | Klein Base, BF16 | 11.1 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-base-int8-convrot.safetensors` | Klein Base, int8 | 5.8 GB |
| `diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-base-nvfp4.safetensors` | Klein Base, NVFP4 | 5.3 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors` | Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder, BF16 | 8.9 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors` | Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct text encoder, int8 | 4.9 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_bf16.safetensors` | prompt upsampler, BF16 | 18.8 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_int8_convrot.safetensors` | prompt upsampler, int8 | 9.8 GB |
| `text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_w4a8.safetensors` | prompt upsampler, w4a8 | 6.7 GB |
| `vae/flux2-vae.safetensors` | image autoencoder | 0.3 GB |

The BF16 transformer and the autoencoder are the same files as `model.safetensors` and `ae.safetensors` on the original repositories. The int8 files run on 8 GB GPUs such as the RTX 3070, and on GPUs without FP8 support (RTX 30 series and older). NVFP4 needs a Blackwell GPU.

## Download

One checkpoint, its text encoder and the autoencoder, straight into the ComfyUI model folders:

```sh
hf download black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-comfy \
  diffusion_models/flux3-image-klein-int8-convrot.safetensors \
  text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_int8_convrot.safetensors \
  vae/flux2-vae.safetensors \
  text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_flux3_prompt_upsampler_in
